Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                           Paper III


Proof. Their quotient is an equivariant orbit-preserving diffeomorphism h. On X \ F it has a
unique expression h(x) = g(x) · x, with g a smooth invariant circle-valued function. We check its
extension across F directly. Choose an equivariant tubular slice and trivialize its normal bundle
locally over F . Conjugating the negative-weight complex coordinate identifies the normal action
with scalar multiplication on C2 . Since h preserves each orbit, it fixes the base variable y and
has normal part
                          (f1 (y, z), f2 (y, z)) = g(y, z)(z1 , z2 ), z 6= 0.
In particular z2 f1 = z1 f2 , an identity of smooth functions also at zero. In the homogeneous Taylor
expansion in the four real normal variables, each pair (p1 , p2 ) therefore satisfies z2 p1 = z1 p2 . In
the complexified polynomial ring with variables z1 , z2 , z̄1 , z̄2 , this implies p1 = z1 q and p2 = z2 q:
first set z1 = 0 and divide by z1 , then cancel z1 . This coefficient argument works with coefficients
depending smoothly on y. It produces a common formal Taylor series for g.
     The formal series can be realized by a smooth complex function G(y, z). Here is the
parametric Borel construction needed for this assertion. On a relatively compact base slice,
write its homogeneous terms as qn (y, z), choose a smooth cutoff equal to one near zero, and
replace each term by χ(z/n )qn (y, z). Choose n ↓ 0 so rapidly that the term and all mixed
base/normal derivatives of total order at most n/2 are bounded by 2−n , away from the finitely
many lower degrees. This is possible because each such derivative retains a positive power of n .
The resulting series converges in every smooth seminorm, and its Taylor series is the prescribed
one: the cutoff is constant near zero and higher homogeneous terms have zero lower jets. This
proves the required local parametric extension. The remainders fj − Gzj are flat in the normal
variables, locally uniformly with all derivatives in y. For z 6= 0,

                                          z̄1 (f1 − Gz1 ) + z̄2 (f2 − Gz2 )
                                g−G=                                        .
                                                         |z|2

A smooth function flat along z = 0, divided by |z|2 , extends smoothly and flatly by zero: the
usual quotient derivative formula and Taylor bounds of arbitrarily high order prove this for every
derivative. Thus g extends smoothly across the slice. Its absolute value is one by continuity.
Equivariance implies invariance on the free part, hence on the slice by continuity. The local
extensions agree because they agree on the dense free stratum. We obtain a global smooth
invariant g : X → S 1 .
    Since X is simply connected, the covering R → S 1 , a 7→ e2πia , gives a smooth lift a. The
integer-valued difference a(λx) − a(x) is zero at λ = 1 and continuous in the connected circle,
so a is invariant. The maps x 7→ e2πisa(x) · x, 0 ≤ s ≤ 1, are diffeomorphisms with the explicit
inverse obtained by changing s to −s. They give the required isotopy.
    For the second assertion the free quotient is a principal circle bundle. A connection lifts the
compactly supported time-dependent vector field of the orbit isotopy to an invariant vector field.
Its flow exists for the full finite time interval, is equivariant, and extends by the identity near
F . The endpoint differs from any other smooth equivariant lift of the same orbit map by the
orbit-preserving diffeomorphism just treated.

Lemma 7.7 (equivariant retraction of the cusp body). For a sufficiently small closed cusp disc
∆, the compact manifold with boundary V = f −1 (∆) has a ρ-equivariant strong deformation

Proposition 7.10 (a nonzero normal Euler number). Glue the two fixed boundary spheres of
Y = dP6 /ρ using their actual conductor identification, and call the resulting closed oriented
three-manifold N . Its natural map to the smooth cusp orbit five-manifold is an immersion. Its
sole self-intersection circle has two disjoint preimage circles, the two pairs of nonfixed edge
intervals of 7.6. Along the fixed sphere F ⊂ N , the oriented normal two-plane bundle of this
immersion has Euler number of absolute value two. If its complex orientation is that of the Hopf
invariant a = xz, where x, z have circle weights +1, −1, the Euler number is −2.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; proposition 7.6.

Proof. Away from the conductor the normalization quotient is embedded. At an ordinary nonfixed
double point the circle acts freely along the double curve, and the two smooth three-dimensional
branches intersect transversely along its one-dimensional orbit quotient. At a fixed double point
the two normal coordinates have weights +1, −1. The Hopf quotient coordinates are

                            a = xz ∈ C,       b = (|x|2 − |z|2 )/2 ∈ R,

together with the coordinate along the fixed curve. The two halves of Y glue as the two signs of
b, so their union is smooth. At a triple point the full base equation is q = xyz, with y tangent
to F and invariant. In the quotient it becomes q = ay. Hence the central orbit fibre is the
union of the two smooth three-planes {a = 0} and {y = 0}, intersecting transversely along the
b-axis. This verifies immersion and transversality at both previously distinguished vertices. The
endpoint identifications of 7.6 join the two nonfixed double arcs into one circle; its preimages in
N are disjoint circles.
    The two complex weight lines in NF /X are each OP1 (−1). To see this with the actual
normalization, each is the normal line of one fixed edge in its dP6 branch, and each edge has
self-intersection −1. This remains true at the two vertices because those branches and their edge
normals are smooth there. The circle characters distinguish the lines globally, so no choice of a
splitting of an extension is required.
    The Hopf invariant a = xz is valued in the tensor product of these two weight lines. It
therefore gives the complex normal line of the branch {a = 0} along F as

                                   O(−1) ⊗ O(−1) = O(−2).

At a triple point q = ay, the coordinate a still is a normal coordinate of that branch. The zero
of y does not alter its normal bundle; using q instead would lose precisely this distinction. The
stated Euler number is consequently −2 for the a-complex orientation and +2 if that normal
orientation is reversed.
    In particular this immersion cannot simply be compressed along F to an immersed three-
sphere while retaining its normal two-plane bundle: extension over a bounding three-disc would
force its Euler pairing on the boundary sphere to vanish. This identifies a required framing
correction; it does not compute that correction or a Haefliger invariant for the annular twist.

Proof. The dimension hypothesis in Fintushel and Pao (1983, Section 1, Propositions 1.3–1.4) is

     Here the orbit identification can be lifted to the claimed equivariant identification. In
the normal bundle of the fixed curve, conjugating the negative weight line converts the circle

+1. The resulting rank-two complex bundle over S 2 has first Chern class zero, and is trivial,
since clutching rank-two complex bundles over S 2 is classified by π1 (U (2)) and its determinant.
Thus its equivariant tubular neighbourhood is the linear model. The oriented normal three-plane
bundle of the orbit sphere is also trivial. The ambient pair diffeomorphism can be adjusted on a
tubular neighbourhood to this prescribed normal model: the relevant change of oriented framing
is a map S 2 → SO(3), and π2 (SO(3)) = 0.

of H 2 (P ; Z), as is seen on each normal Hopf sphere. Choose the orbit identification to match this
signed generator with the linear model. Principal circle bundles are classified by that class, so
their complements are equivariantly isomorphic. On the common boundary the difference from
the prescribed tubular isomorphism is a gauge S 2 × S 2 → S 1 . It has a real logarithm because
H 1 (S 2 × S 2 ; Z) = 0. Extending that logarithm over a collar and using a cutoff corrects the
bundle isomorphism there. The two isomorphisms now glue smoothly. This proof uses the linear
tubular model at the fixed set; it does not assume that an arbitrary quotient diffeomorphism
lifts smoothly there.

of P preserves the meridian Euler class, since restriction H 2 (P ) → H 2 (∂P ) is injective. It
therefore has a circle-bundle lift, which can be made the identity on a boundary collar by the

from the fixed-disc normal products. Framed surgery fills that boundary by a third copy of
N . Combine this third copy with one of the first two along its inner P . Two four-discs glued
along a boundary three-disc form a four-disc. The combined piece is therefore again N , and the
remaining gluing map is ψ on the outer half and the identity on the inner half. This is exactly
the displayed Mψ , with the boundary orientation convention used there.

For 0 ≤ a ≤ 1 replace C(q) by (1 − a)C(q), keeping the same A2 triangulation and the real
periods w, δ. This is a deformation of the actual toric period quotient, not a replacement inferred
from its homology. The two period automorphisms still have the same integral translations of the

their leading part is (Im s)B0 , while the remaining matrices are uniformly bounded.
    The fixed toric charts, with this extra parameter, therefore give a smooth family of the
same Mumford cusp quotients. There is no new stabilizer at the central fibre: a nonzero period
translates every height-one ray by a nonzero lattice vector, and cannot preserve any finite cone
of the fan. The usual finite fundamental collection of toric charts gives proper discontinuity,
uniformly for the compact parameter interval. The central family has the constant compact
normalization dP6 with its smoothly varying opposite-side identifications. Thus it has a proper
representative over a uniform smaller q-disc. One may see the uniformity directly by taking a
relatively compact neighbourhood of this compact central family: its boundary is disjoint from
q = 0, and after shrinking |q| no fibre meets that boundary. The nonzero fibres are connected
compact tori, so the selected representative contains the whole nearby fibre. Denote these
compact smooth cusp bodies by Va .

conjugating the negative-weight line the normal representation is scalar multiplication on C2 .
Choose Hermitian metrics and a unitary connection, and make the transport linear and unitary
in these normal coordinates. The collar and fixed tubes are disjoint. A circle-invariant partition
of unity extends and patches the prescribed horizontal fields; each has derivative one on a, so
their patched field does also. Compactness gives its flow for the entire interval.
    This particular transport induces a smooth transport of orbit spaces. On the free locus this
follows from the principal-bundle quotient. In the fixed tubes, unitary normal transport induces
the usual smooth linear rotation in the Hopf R3 coordinates. Thus it is smooth there as well.
This explicit choice avoids any assertion that every equivariant smooth map has a smooth map
in an arbitrarily preassigned quotient atlas. The Hopf smooth structures and tubular choices are
legitimate ones for the orbit construction in 7.13; the annular map is supported in the free collar,
where these structures coincide. We obtain a marked orbit diffeomorphism

Remark 7.18 (Scope). The raw fractional period translations need not extend across the central
fibre. The action above modifies their interior orbits. Its loop moves the fixed sphere, which
is exactly the feature retained by the annular relative mapping class. Thus the construction
does not trivialize that class or evaluate Jψ . In particular the nonbounding three-torus prevents
discarding its stable framing contribution by a chain lying entirely in the cusp body.

Proposition 7.27 (an additive integer before reduction modulo 28). Fix the linear semifree
circle action of 7.13, with its circle direction fixed. On the group of orientation-preserving
equivariant diffeomorphisms of S 6 there is an integer

                                      q : π0 Diff+
                                                 S1
                                                    (S 6 ) −→ Z

defined by the unframed Haefliger coordinate of the orbit three-knot of equivariant clutching.
It is a group homomorphism. For a representative normalized to be the identity on a fixed
tubular neighbourhood, it is Wall’s unframed knot coordinate, so q = −J in the convention
of 7.13. Its image in the ordinary group Θ7 is the fixed signed reduction modulo 28 described
there. In particular, if an equivariant representative has a sixth power equivariantly isotopic to a
representative with J = 0 as an integer, its ordinary mapping class is zero.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; proposition 7.13; Smale (1959,
Theorem A, page 621); (Haefliger, 1966, Sections 1 and 5.16); Davis (1982, Example 7.14 and
Proposition 7.15).

Proof. We first make the normalization and its independence explicit. The fixed set is F = S 2 , and
its equivariant normal bundle is the trivial scalar complex rank-two bundle after conjugating the
negative weight, by 7.13. An equivariant real derivative on that normal representation is complex
linear and has positive real determinant. An orientation-preserving ambient diffeomorphism
therefore restricts to an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of F .
    By Smale (1959, Theorem A, page 621), this restriction is isotopic to the identity. Lift such an
isotopy using the product normal bundle and an invariant tubular cutoff, extending its velocity
field equivariantly. After this adjustment the map fixes F pointwise. Its normal derivative is
a map F → GL2 (C). Polar decomposition and π2 (U (2)) = 0 give a homotopy to the identity,
again realized in the fixed tube by an equivariant isotopy. Finally the usual rescaling of a tubular
germ to its derivative, followed by an invariant cutoff, makes the whole map the identity on a
smaller fixed tube. Equivariance rules out a derivative from the nontrivial normal representation
to the fixed tangent representation; the rescaled germ is smooth at the zero parameter. This
normalization uses equivariant isotopies throughout.
    Clutch two standard linear equivariant seven-discs by this diffeomorphism. Their fixed
three-discs clutch to S 3 . Their orbit six-discs clutch to a homotopy six-sphere, which is standard
because Θ6 = 0. The fixed image is thus a smooth oriented three-knot in S 6 . Its Haefliger
integer is the proposed q, using the connected-sum group of oriented three-knots in the six-sphere
(Haefliger, 1966, Sections 1 and 5.16).
    This integer does not depend on the chosen normalization. An equivariant isotopy of boundary
clutching maps extends over a collar to a diffeomorphism of the clutched equivariant pairs. The
resulting orbit pairs are diffeomorphic. One can choose compatible unitary normal tubes along
the entire isotopy, so that their Hopf orbit charts form a smooth family; this does not invoke
functorial smoothness for arbitrary equivariant maps in a fixed raw quotient atlas. There is also
no ambiguity from identifying the orbit homotopy sphere with S 6 . An orientation-preserving
diffeomorphism of S 6 is isotopic to one supported in a ball disjoint from a given compact three-
knot: make its germ the identity near a point, use stereographic coordinates on the complement,
and conjugate its compact support into a small ball by translations and positive dilations,
all isotopic to the identity. Such a representative fixes that knot. Consequently the ambient
identification cannot change its knot integer.
    We prove additivity geometrically. Normalize two equivariant diffeomorphisms to be the
identity near F . In particular each is the identity near a chosen fixed point. Stereographic
projection from that point identifies the complement with R2 ⊕ C2 , with the circle acting scalarly
on the second summand. The diffeomorphism has compact support there. Positive dilations
and translations along the fixed R2 commute with the circle and are equivariantly isotopic to

                                                380
Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                     Paper III


the identity on the one-point compactification. By conjugation, place the two supports inside
disjoint small invariant balls centered at distinct fixed points. The resulting maps remain in their
original equivariant components.
    For disjoint supports, the composition clutch is the equivariant connected sum of the two
separate clutches. This follows directly by cutting the equatorial sphere between the two invariant
balls and inserting a product collar; the map on the separating collar is the identity. The fixed
three-discs undergo the same boundary connected-sum operation. On the orbit pairs this is the
ordinary connected sum of the two oriented three-knots. The defining group operation of their
Haefliger integers is connected sum. Hence

                                       q(φ1 φ2 ) = q(φ1 ) + q(φ2 ).

This proves additivity without passing first to Θ7 .
    For a fixed-tube-relative representative, the surgery cap and Wall calculation of 7.13 apply
verbatim: the inherited product normal framing gives q = −J. Altering this framing changes
only Wall’s framing coordinate, whose equivariant lift extends over the seven-disc by the explicit
quaternionic formula in 7.13. Finally the orbit-knot generator comparison of Davis (1982,
Example 7.14 and Proposition 7.15) identifies the underlying ordinary sphere class with the fixed
signed reduction of q modulo 28.
    If φ6 is equivariantly isotopic to a representative with integer J = 0, then 6q(φ) = 0 in Z.
Thus q(φ) = 0, and its underlying ordinary mapping class is zero. This last implication uses
a torsion-free integer before reduction; it is not inferred from the weaker equation 6[φ] = 0 in
Z/28.

Proposition 7.31 (direct characteristic-index additivity). For a fixed-tube-relative orbit
diffeomorphism ϕ of the linear semifree sphere, form its actual surgery cap Mϕ and meridian
line Lx as in the geometric construction of 7.13. Define
                                             1
                                    λ(ϕ) =      hp1 (Mϕ )x − 4x3 , [Mϕ ]i.
                                             24
This integer is additive under composition. It is unchanged by the equivariant isotopies and
fixed-tube normalizations of the upstairs diffeomorphism, and therefore defines an integer on
its equivariant mapping class. These conclusions follow directly from spin index theory and
characteristic bordisms; they do not use the classification or integer of three-knots, Wall’s surgery
formula, or the comparison of a knot generator with a Milnor sphere.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; proposition 7.13; proposition 7.23;
Smale (1959, Theorem A).

Proof. The geometric cap is a simply connected spin six-manifold with H 2 = H 4 = Z and H 3 = 0.
These facts follow from the explicit two-copy construction N ∪ϕe (−N ), N = S 2 × D4 , by van
Kampen, Mayer–Vietoris and the unique boundary spin structure. They do not require a knot
classification. The twisted spin Dirac formula gives

                         ind(D ⊗ Lx ) = hx3 /6 − p1 x/24, [Mϕ ]i = −λ(ϕ),

so the displayed quantity is an integer.
    We first prove additivity for maps fixed on the chosen tube. Put Y = ∂N = DP = S 2 × S 3
and extend each map by the identity on the second half. The meridian line on Y has a lift of
each extended map: the actual upstairs circle bundle provides it on P , and the identity provides
it on the other half. Their boundary values agree. Choose the lift of a composition to be the
composition of these lifts.
    An oriented pair of pants has free fundamental group on its two incoming boundary generators.
The two diffeomorphisms therefore specify a smooth Y -bundle over that surface, with outgoing
boundary monodromy their composition. The chosen line bundle lifts specify a line bundle on
its total space. This total space is a compact oriented seven-manifold whose boundary is the

                                                     385
Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                     Paper III


outgoing mapping torus minus the two incoming mapping tori. Its stable tangent bundle restricts
to their tangent bundles plus the outward normal line. Consequently both characteristic numbers
x3 and p1 x are additive on these mapping tori, by bordism invariance.
    Use the explicit seven-manifold of proposition 7.23: a Y -bundle over an annulus with
monodromy the doubled map, with two N × [0, 1] pieces attached over opposite outer arcs. The
remaining outer arcs produce the twisted and identity doubles, and the inner circle produces the
mapping torus. The chosen line lift on the annular bundle and the pullback lines on the attached
pieces agree on their attaching faces. Thus this is an actual bordism carrying both the meridian
line and its tangent bundle, not merely a relation between abstract intersection matrices. Its
boundary orientations compare a cap minus the identity cap with the mapping torus, with one
sign that is independent of the map. The identity cap S 2 × S 4 and identity mapping torus have
zero x3 and zero p1 x. Applying the same sign to all three boundary terms of the pair-of-pants
bordism proves that x3 and p1 x are individually additive for fixed-tube-relative maps. Their
displayed integral combination is therefore additive as well. In particular the proof does not infer
additivity from a three-knot group law. The line class is unambiguous here: H 1 (Y ; Z) = 0, so
changing its specified lift by a gauge does not add a mixed mapping-torus Chern class.
    It remains to check normalization choices. An orientation- preserving equivariant sphere
diffeomorphism can be made the identity on a fixed tube by equivariant isotopies: its fixed S 2
restriction is isotopic to the identity by Smale (1959, Theorem A); its complex normal derivative
is homotopic to the identity since π2 (U (2)) = 0; and tubular rescaling removes the remaining
higher-order germ. These are the local geometric steps, independent of any three-knot invariant.
    Two such normalizations give equivariantly diffeomorphic clutched sphere pairs. Extend their
boundary isotopy over a collar to obtain the diffeomorphism. Compatible unitary normal tubes
along the isotopy give compatible smooth orbit structures. Thus their orbit pairs are the same
smooth pair up to diffeomorphism. The fixed image is a three-sphere and its oriented normal
three-plane bundle is trivial. The two inherited normal framings differ by a map r : S 3 → SO(3).
    We compute directly the change caused by this framing. If E is the exterior of the embedded
three-sphere, its two framed surgeries fill E by S 2 × D4 with boundary identifications differing by
                            (a, z) 7−→ (r(z)a, z),       (a, z) ∈ S 2 × S 3 .
Cutting off the common exterior gives a characteristic bordism between the difference of these
two surgery caps and
                              Zr = (S 2 × D4 ) ∪r −(S 2 × D4 ),
which is the oriented sphere bundle S(ηr ) → S 4 of the rank-three bundle clutched by r. The
meridian lines extend over this bordism. They agree on the common boundary, and their possible
gauge discrepancy has a real logarithm because H 1 (S 2 × S 3 ; Z) = 0.
    Let π : Zr → S 4 and choose x with positive fibre evaluation one. The oriented vertical
tangent two-plane has Euler class 2x, since H 2 (Zr ; Z) = Z and its Euler evaluation on the fibre
is two. Its stable isomorphism Tvert Zr ⊕ R ≃ π ∗ ηr gives

Remark 7.33 (Independence and shared geometric inputs). The first determination uses the

invokes the first determination. The two methods share the proved annular representative

Remark 7.34 (Established surgery and index machinery). The Hopf-handle construction used

in his oriented decomposition conventions. 7.29 supplies the direct calculation with general cubic

surgery construction or invariant formula is claimed.
    The relation between semifree actions, fixed three-sphere knots, and surgery to homotopy
complex projective three-spaces is classical. The primary introduction of Montgomery and Yang
(1968, pp. 125–126) describes these correspondences and the Pontryagin offset divisible by 24.
The second proof here derives its needed additivity and framing independence from the explicit
bordisms and the vertical Euler identity; it does not import the knot classification as a premise.
This identifies both the standard literature and the exact scope of the derivation.

The projection formula and its missing inputs. The current literature supplies another
precise test for a proposed orbit-knot computation. Theorem 4.1 of Gauniyal and Turchin (2026),
published online on 25 September 2026, expresses the Haefliger integer using both double-point
linking and invariants of the projected immersion. The latter include a rationally normalized
Smale invariant. Consequently the double circle of 7.17 alone is insufficient. An application here
would require an actual compressed projection and its tangent-framing comparison. We opened
the published formula and its definitions, rather than importing the linking term in isolation.
    Likewise, Sakai (2015, Theorem 2.5) computes the change under a specified crossing change
from oriented double-preimage linking. To obtain an absolute value by that route one must also
identify the comparison embedding and its class. Neither formula identifies the present trace
with a standard reference embedding. The characteristic-number cap retains those geometric
comparisons as explicit requirements. Searches on 15 November 2026 for the six-sphere family,
its degeneration monodromy, and these knot formulas did not locate a numerical determination
for this particular family. This states the search outcome.

circle. An antiholomorphic map in complex dimension three reverses the real orientation because

Proof. The proper submersion has a smooth horizontal distribution; integration along a compact
path exists because the fibres are compact. The complex orientation varies continuously. Its
monodromy therefore preserves the orientation class in H 6 and fixes the constant class in H 0 .
These are the only nonzero integral cohomology groups, proving the first assertion with integral

    Since e−πi(c0 −2r) = e−πic0 e2πir , the path c(r) is the lift of the positive circle. The descent
gluing at its endpoint is exactly F2,c0 −2 , proving (E9). A path of horizontal distributions gives
a smooth path of the resulting monodromy diffeomorphisms, so their isotopy classes agree.
Changing the coherent descent maps by a member of the connected automorphism group also
leaves this class unchanged. The diffeomorphism Xc0 ≃ S 6 is chosen with the complex orientation.
    The glued manifold ΣΦ is simply connected by van Kampen and has the integral homology
of S 7 by Mayer–Vietoris; the Hurewicz and Whitehead arguments give a homotopy sphere.
The gluing comparison π0 Diff+ (S 6 ) = Θ7 sends Φ to this construction. Here we use Cerf’s
sphere-gluing comparison in dimension six (Cerf, 1970, Theorem 0 and Corollaries 1–2, p. 8):
isotopy classes are the group of sphere gluing maps modulo extension over a disc. The extension
equivalence is exactly the equivalence of their two-disc gluings. In dimension seven, the simply
connected h-cobordism comparison identifies these classes with oriented homotopy spheres; the
comparison with oriented diffeomorphism classes is Smale’s Theorem J (Smale, 1961, pp. 393–394).
Thus the map being evaluated is the actual boundary gluing of (E9). Eells–Kuiper’s seven-
dimensional invariant is (p21 − 4σ)/896 modulo one and distinguishes the twenty-eight oriented
homotopy-seven-sphere classes (Eells and Kuiper, 1962, Section 6, equation (11), pp. 101–103).
Multiplying that formula by twenty-eight gives (E10). Its hypotheses hold here: a homotopy
seven-sphere is spin and has vanishing H 3 (−; Q) and H 4 (−; Q), so the relative lift is unique.

Remark 8.2 (Resolution of the original compact-filling and mapping-class questions). The
original question asked for a flat proper filling of the compact S 6 family over w = 0. The specific
equivariant compactification is excluded by Paper I, Paper I, Theorem 21.58. In particular no

could be asserted. Paper I, Proposition 19.6 constructs and computes the two reduced-surface
degenerations after the stated additional base change; it does not construct a neighbourhood of
the nonreduced fibres 3S1 and 4S2 in a compact limit.
    The finite-place test in that question was the extension of the order-three affine deck action
over a two-parameter plumbing in (t, s), with prescribed normal character and central multiplicity
three, followed by descent from s to w = s6 . The order-four analogue must retain the normal
character of order four. At infinity the prescribed periodic gluing was the one specified in Paper I,
Remark 19.5, now compatible with these finite-place quotients. The computed central surface
homology groups cannot be substituted for the homology of that unconstructed threefold.
    For the mapping-class part, E.2.2 gives the exact clutching map and its characteristic-
number reduction. The complete characteristic and boundary calculations in theorem 7.28 and
corollary 7.32 give zero for this particular ΣΦ . The numeric instance to be evaluated was the
residue (E10) for the single loop based at c0 = −i(M + 1); all other basepoints in the connected
parameter disc give conjugate monodromy, and Θ7 is abelian. The identity on cohomology alone
does not evaluate that residue; the complete cap calculations do.

The central normalization and conductor. Multiplication by N fixes every ray of Σ. It therefore
maps a chosen source component of the toric central fibre to the corresponding target component.
The star of that ray is the hexagonal fan, so the restriction is the toric power map [N ] : dP6 → dP6 .
On its dense two-torus it has degree N 2 ; in each toric boundary chart it is an N th-power map in
the normal coordinate, hence has ramification index N along all six boundary curves. Equation
(20) says that the source and target lattice identifications commute with this map. Consequently
opposite boundary curves, their conductor identifications, and the two translation-orbits of
triangle vertices descend compatibly. This proves (15) and completes the proof.

Remark 9.2 (Why the unmodified action does not work). If one reuses the target action with v
in place of t at the source, then the two sides of equivariance have multiplicative factors

                                 cλ̄ (v)N v N B0 λ̄   and cλ̄ (v N )v N B0 λ̄ ,

respectively. In general cλ̄ (v)N 6= cλ̄ (v N ). Thus the bare formula (ξ1 , ξ2 , v) 7→ (ξ1N , ξ2N , v N )
extends on the ambient toric variety but does not descend through the manuscript’s quotient
unless the source factor (8) is inserted. The explicit logarithm 2πiC(v N )λ̄/N makes this root
holomorphic; no unjustified choice of an N th root is involved.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; equation (8).

Remark 9.3 (Exact scope). The theorem constructs a finite morphism of completed families
over the local cusp discs. It is a degree-N 3 map to the original family and a degree-N 2 map only
after the target is base changed. It is neither a degree-N 2 self-map over the unchanged disc nor
the normalization of the base change.

sends ub to a vector whose w-

                                   b             are −1 and 1. A further global base cover and
compatible extensions through both finite fillings would have to be constructed separately. The
local Kummer morphism also supplies no map to a product sphere, smash sphere, S 12 , or S 24 .

    For completeness, Borel–Serre prove that S 2n admits no almost-complex structure for n ≥ 4.
Their argument applies to every differentiable structure on the sphere: on S 2n , all lower Chern
classes vanish, while their reduced-power calculation forces the top Chern class to vanish modulo
a suitable odd prime p < n; on the other hand that class is the Euler class, namely 2h for
a generator h ∈ H 2n (S 2n ; Z), a contradiction. Taking n = 6 and n = 12 gives the asserted
obstructions for S 12 and S 24 . This topological obstruction does not itself prohibit the real
four-circle target GT , the target-smash S 4 , or their metric limits.
    Finally, X ∗ X ∼  = S 13 and X ∗4 ∼= S 27 , so joins do not produce the proposed S 12 or S 24
dimensions. Suspensions can produce spheres of those dimensions only by discarding the torus-
fibration maps.

9.3    Cone-compactified sphere carriers for the native cusp quotient
This subsection answers a topological question which is strictly different from the finite-cover
construction. No period is enlarged by passing to a cover. Instead, the native expanding quotient
is retained on the cusp, the parts on which that quotient is unavailable are collapsed, and the
resulting based map is passed through a smash product. The outcome is an exact global map
with source S 12 , and there is an analogous S 24 map from the full-monodromy-invariant circle
quotient. The targets are conically stratified spaces. The Euclidean limits below use the intrinsic
metrics inherited from the flat quotient tori on the regular slices; they are not ambient metric
limits in one fixed metric on the compact targets.

Proof. Every neighborhood of the relevant cone vertex contains every sufficiently small radial
cross-section, uniformly in all compact angular and torus coordinates. In a compatible metric,
every such cross-section eventually lies in an arbitrarily small ball about the vertex. Products
followed by the smash quotient preserve this uniform convergence, proving equation (102).
    For a flat torus with systole s, choose a shortest primitive period λ. The class of λ/2 has
distance s/2 from zero: for every period µ, the nonzero period λ − 2µ has length at least s. Hence
the diameter is at least s/2. Equations equation (69) and equation (96) prove equation (103).

track the lifted metric, and determine the topology of the resulting total space. No such smooth
compact sphere construction follows from the present data.

9.3.1   Optimal sphere exponents and the exact Euclidean boundary

Within the class of native connected fibrewise torus quotients equipped with the induced, unscaled
quotient of the marked Euclidean metric, the two sphere dimensions in the preceding constructions
are forced by two different integral quotient problems. Cusp-locally, each copy has an expanding
quotient of rank two, so two copies are necessary and sufficient within that class. Over the full
regular base, monodromy leaves at most one expanding quotient direction per copy, so four
copies are necessary and sufficient within the same class. We now prove this scoped optimality,
identify the compact conical carriers, and construct a noncompact comparison manifold in which
the limiting R4 is an actual boundary fibre. There is only a continuous comparison map from

                                                 416
Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                      Paper III


this manifold to the compact conical carrier: it set-theoretically collapses the new boundary, is a
homeomorphism away from that boundary, and is nonproper and nonquotient.

centers are suppressed.

Remark 9.19 (The moving four-spheres are null-homotopic in the targets). For a fixed interior
reduced-suspension coordinate, the inclusion ST2 ,→ S 3 contracts through based maps by sliding
that coordinate to a suspension endpoint; throughout the homotopy the collapsed meridian
remains at the global basepoint. Hence ST2 ∧ ST2 ,→ S 6 is null-homotopic. The identical sliding
argument contracts CT ,→ S 2 , and therefore also contracts CT∧4 ,→ S 8 . Thus the moving metric
four-spheres do not contradict the fixed-target orientation obstruction: their fundamental classes
die in the ambient targets.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; the argument and qualifications
immediately following.

Remark 9.20 (Homotopical status of the two sphere-to-sphere maps). The maps S 12 → S 6
and S 24 → S 8 induce zero on all positive-degree integral homology and cohomology groups
and have zero ordinary Hurewicz image. They have no classical degree because source and
target dimensions differ. The full four-copy map qbγ∧4 : S 24 → S 8 is based null-homotopic by
corollary 9.17. The distinct two-copy map qb3∧2 : S 12 → S 6 is also based null-homotopic, by
corollary 9.16. In both cases the vanishing is a theorem about the full specified sphere-valued
map, not merely its Hurewicz image or the inclusion of a moving four-sphere. The one-copy
class [b
       q3 ] ∈ π6 (S 3 ) is zero by the complete framed-torus proof in theorem 9.29. Both this class
and [bqγ ] ∈ π6 (S 2 ) also vanish by the extension homotopy in proposition 9.43. That proof uses
the original formulas after forgetting the base angle and fixes the chosen point of the central
fibre throughout. It supplies based nullhomotopies of all their positive smash powers. The
retained-angle map has a different target and is outside that assertion.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; corollary 9.17; corollary 9.16;
theorem 9.29; proposition 9.43.

countable base of the quotient.

Corollary 9.24 (Sharp global meaning of the Euclidean limit). The native routes constructed
above exhibit the underlying space R4 in the following three precise senses:

   1. as each of the nonclosed topologically embedded open cells U12,T ⊂ S 6 and U24,T ⊂ S 8 ;

   2. as the pointed intrinsic Euclidean limit of the four-torus slices in the global quotient carriers
      of S 12 and S 24 ; and

   3. as the Euclidean decompactification boundary fibre of E12 and E24 .

It does not produce R4 as the whole compact sphere, as the whole compact conical target, or as a
continuous quotient target of either compact space. Nor does the unrescaled restriction of any
fixed compatible ambient target metric have R4 as its slice limit, and the open cells in item 1 are
not globally Euclidean-isometric in such a metric.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; corollary 9.18; proposition 9.21;
theorem 9.23; equation (132); theorem 9.32.

Proof. The three positive assertions are corollary 9.18 and proposition 9.21 and theorem 9.23.
For the negative assertions, a continuous image of a compact sphere or compact conical target is
compact, so it cannot be all of R4 . The local homology calculation equation (132) shows that the
carrier vertex is not an integral homology-manifold point, and hence not a manifold point, of any
dimension, with or without boundary. Finally, in every fixed compatible metric on a compact
cone target, all sufficiently deep radial slices lie uniformly in an arbitrarily small neighborhood
of the vertex, so their ambient diameters tend to zero. Their intrinsic diameters tend to infinity
because their intrinsic systoles do. Hence without a T -dependent rescaling no fixed ambient
metric realizes the intrinsic Euclidean limit on those slices. The fixed cusp-adapted blow-ups are
treated separately in theorem 9.32. The comparison diagrams record the unrescaled distinction
exactly: they collapse the new R4 boundary rather than identify it with the compact target.

Scope. The constructions above use only the original, unscaled fibre metrics and the quotient
maps derived from the native S 6 cusp. They do not use the auxiliary finite-cover unspooling. The
conical carriers depend on the chosen cusp coordinate, positive radial ray, and based identification
X∼ = S 6 . The spaces Eν additionally remember the marked Euclidean quotient metrics. None
of these data defines a compact complex structure on S 12 or S 24 , a four-dimensional physical
spacetime, or an interacting Yang–Mills Hamiltonian.

Theorem 9.25 (The full external smash pairing is zero). For every pair of based maps x, y :
S6 → S3,
                             [x ∧ y] = 0   in     π12 (S 6 ).
In particular, qb3∧2 : S 12  S 6 is simultaneously surjective as a point-set quotient and based
null-homotopic.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; (Hatcher, 2002a, opening table,
p. 339); (Isaksen et al., 2023, Table 1, p. 113); equation (138).

Proof. Write E for reduced suspension, using the ordered smash coordinates on spheres. The
external smash product has the exact factorization

                x ∧ y = (x ∧ idS 3 ) ◦ (idS 6 ∧y) : S 6 ∧ S 6 −→ S 6 ∧ S 3 −→ S 3 ∧ S 3 .      (137)

Under the displayed ordered sphere identifications, the two factors, in order of application,
represent E 6 y ∈ π12 (S 9 ) and E 3 x ∈ π9 (S 6 ). Equivalently, Toda’s Barratt–Hilton reduced-join
formula gives, with p = q = k = h = 3,

                                     [x ∧ y] = (E 3 [x]) ◦ (E 6 [y]).                          (138)

Here Toda’s sign is (−1)(p+k)h = (−1)18 = +1. Reversing the two displayed factors introduces
the separate twist sign (−1)ph = −1; no such reversal is used here.
   The three exact groups needed below are

                    π6 (S 3 ) ∼
                              = Z/12,      π12 (S 9 ) ∼
                                                      = Z/24,       π12 (S 6 ) ∼
                                                                               = Z/2.          (139)

The first and third are the integral low unstable groups displayed in Hatcher’s table extracted
from Toda; the middle group is in the stable three-stem (Hatcher, 2002a, opening table, p. 339);
(Isaksen et al., 2023, Table 1, p. 113).
    Put β = E 6 [y] ∈ π12 (S 9 ). Since 12[y] = 0, functoriality of suspension gives 12β = 0. In
the cyclic group Z/24, the elements annihilated by 12 are exactly the even elements. Hence
there is γ ∈ π12 (S 9 ) such that β = 2γ. Postcomposition with E 3 [x] : S 9 → S 6 induces a group
homomorphism
                                   (E 3 [x])∗ : π12 (S 9 ) −→ π12 (S 6 ).
The target has exponent two, so equation (138) gives

                             [x ∧ y] = (E 3 [x])∗ (β) = 2(E 3 [x])∗ (γ) = 0.

This proves the vanishing of the entire external smash pairing and hence the theorem.

is a framing of the normal three-plane bundle of W, and its restriction to the collar is exactly
the framing N P from (156), with every original target-coordinate sign retained. Concatenate
the framing cylinder of the preceding paragraph with this nullbordism, rescaling the two interval
lengths. Their framings agree exactly on the common product collar, so the concatenation is a
smooth framed nullbordism of the actual inverse image.

4. The based map represented by this framed inverse image. Choose the injective
chart to exclude x0 if its center is not x0 . If its center is x0 , the constructed nullbordism still
excludes x0 , since |w1 | = ρ1 > 0 and |w2 | = ρ2 > 0 everywhere on it. Compactness therefore
gives tubular neighborhoods for the framed cylinder and cap disjoint from {x0 } × [0, 1].
    The original continuous quotient map is smooth and a submersion near its entire inverse
image of y0 . First make it constant in a neighborhood of x0 , by a based homotopy that changes
nothing near that inverse image. Explicitly, take a target chart κ : O → R3 with κ(∗) = 0, whose
image is a ball, and y0 ∈ / O. By continuity choose a neighborhood U of x0 with g(U ) ⊂ O, and
a smooth bump function β supported in U and equal to one near x0 . For x ∈ U , replace g(x)
during this homotopy by κ−1 ((1 − aβ(x))κ(g(x))), 0 ≤ a ≤ 1, and leave g fixed off U . Convexity
of the target chart image makes the formula well-defined, the vanishing of β near the boundary
of its support proves continuity of the pasted formula, and κ(g(x0 )) = 0 makes the homotopy
based. It never introduces an inverse image of y0 . Its endpoint is smooth near x0 and agrees
with g near the entire old inverse image.


                                                   436
Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                      Paper III


    Denote the endpoint of the preceding homotopy by gb . Choose one closed tubular neighborhood
U1 of the inverse image, contained in the smooth submersion region and with the entire inverse
image contained in int U1 . The compact set X \ int U1 has image under gb missing y0 . In a fixed
target metric put
                                 d0 = min d(gb (x), y0 ) > 0.
                                         x∈X\int U1

Relative smooth approximation, fixed on the whole closed set U1 and on a neighborhood of x0 ,
gives a smooth based representative gsm whose error on X \ int U1 is less than d0 /2. It therefore
has the same inverse image and differential on U1 , and d(gsm (x), y0 ) > d0 /2 on its complement.
Thus there is no uncontrolled intervening region and no additional inverse image. Make the
approximation also closer than a fixed target injectivity radius; its short geodesics give the based
homotopy.
    The relative Pontryagin construction now applies to the explicit framed nullbordism. It
produces a based homotopy to a map missing y0 ; stereographic contraction of S 3 \ {y0 } ∼   = R3 to
the image of ∗ is based and contracts that last map. For completeness, the dependence on the
framed inverse image in this argument is precisely the local product-neighborhood construction
and the interpolation lemma of (Milnor, 1965b, §7, Theorem B and Lemma 4, pp. 43, 48–50).
Their relative versions fix the source basepoint because all tubular modifications are away from it
and stereographic interpolation between equal values keeps that value fixed. A framed cylinder
realizes a framing homotopy; the empty Pontryagin manifold realizes a map missing the chosen
regular value. This proves the claimed based null-homotopy of the exact map g.

Corollary 9.30. Under the original fixed based identification X ∼
                                                                = S 6 , the one-copy coefficient is

       [g] = 0 ∈ π6 (S 3 ) ∼

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; the explicit constructions and

Proof. The theorem states that the actual based map is null-homotopic. Precomposition with the

the unique coefficient of [g] in any generator of Z/12 is zero. For every [n], Θg ([n]) = n · 0 = 0,
and every composite with this homomorphism is zero.

Exact scope. The proof computes this sphere-valued postcomposition. It does not compute
the homotopy class of the earlier conical-target map q2 : X → Susp(S 1 × T ), and it does not
                                                                               2

assert a null-homotopy for that different target. Point-set surjectivity of g and all of its stated
metric restrictions remain properties of the original map: a homotopy-class computation does
not alter the defining formula (144). The retained-angle companion is proved separately in

12ν6 6= 0 in π9 (S 6 ). These positive computations use the actual four-framed inverse torus of

through pb2 .

convergence confined to this regular-stratum exhaustion.

Corollary 9.34 (Unit-volume normalization does not give R4 ). The four-volume of Q2T is
(det YT )2 ∼ T 4 . Its unit-volume length factor is therefore (det YT )−1/2 ∼ T −1 , and its unit-
volume limit is a square flat four-torus, not R4 . Likewise, the four-volume of CT4 is `4T , and its
unit-volume normalization is exactly the square unit four-torus.

immediately following.

   An exact metric cone is invariant under every radial blow-up at its vertex, and its Hausdorff
dimension is one plus that of its fixed piecewise-Riemannian link. For the first target,

                              H8 Cone(T 3 ∗ T 3 ), T 3 ∗ T 3 ; Z ∼

the analogous top local group for the B target is Z in degree 12, while the full C calculation is

is R4 . The diameter calculation proves the final assertion.

Consequences for the three sphere routes. The exact positive statement is that one
fixed metric on each compact codomain contains the native R4 decompactification as a vertical
four-plane in a moving-point Euclidean bubble. The whole bubbles are R8 for the S 12 route and
R12 for the S 24 routes. The factor βT = λT rT proves that this dimension discrepancy cannot be
removed by a different scalar rescaling of the same fixed cusp-adapted metric: the slice unrolls
only when the smash base point has already gone to infinite scaled distance.
    No metric on a source sphere is supplied by these quotient constructions. If an independent
smooth Riemannian metric is placed on S 12 or S 24 , its ordinary tangent spaces are R12 or R24 .
Pulling a codomain metric back through q2∧2 or q1∧4 , on the regular strata where the maps are
differentiable, gives a degenerate quadratic form along the positive-dimensional quotient kernels,
not a Riemannian source metric.
    The moving four-sphere carriers

                          S412,T = ST2 ∧ ST2 ⊂ S 6 ,         S424,T = CT∧4 ⊂ S 8

of theorem 9.15 carry separately assigned metrics. Namely, ST2 first receives the quotient length
metric obtained from (T , hT ) ∼   = (QT , gQT ) by collapsing K (1) ⊂ T , equivalently by collapsing
                           2                                             2

ιT (K (1) ) ⊂ QT . Then S412,T receives the quotient length metric of the Riemannian `2 -product
(ST2 )2 after its fat wedge is collapsed. Likewise, S424,T receives the quotient length metric of the
Riemannian `2 -product CT4 after its fat wedge is collapsed. These metrics are assigned directly
to the moving carriers; they are unrescaled intrinsic quotient metrics, not restrictions of D12 or
  B , whose domains are the conical targets, and no fixed ambient metric on S 6 or S 8 is used to

Proof. In the coordinate chart, the stable tangent trivialization is the isomorphism

             R4 ⊕ T M −→ T C3 |M ,        (v, V ) 7−→ v1 N` + v2 Nφ + v3 N1 + v4 N2 + V.

Using the intrinsic frame (−∂a , ∂b ) on T M , its matrix is precisely (210). The homotopy (211)
therefore makes this comparison constant. A constant positive matrix changes no homotopy class

of determinant one can be reduced to the identity by finitely many oriented plane rotations, each
joined to the identity by varying its angle. This proves the asserted comparison within the chart.
    It remains to compare the chart with the ambient sphere framing. Pull back the usual stable
tangent trivialization T S 6 ⊕ R ∼= R7 under the fixed based diffeomorphism X ∼       = S 6 . On the
contractible w-ball containing M , it differs from the coordinate trivialization plus one real line by
a continuous map into GL(7, R). Contracting the ball to its center contracts this comparison map
to a constant. Thus its restriction to M contributes no varying stable framing class. If the chosen
sphere orientation disagrees with the complex orientation, the remaining constant has negative
determinant and reverses the resulting framed bordism class. Both that sign and the explicit sign
(208) disappear in the order-two class computed below. This argument compares actual ambient
trivializations on a contractible chart; it does not suppose that C3 globally trivializes T X.

Nonzero framed bordism and the exact unstable class We give the nonvanishing test
for the resulting torus explicitly. A stable framing gives a spin structure by lifting its oriented
frame to the trivial Spin-bundle. On the Lie-framed circle this is the disconnected double cover,
whereas the spin structure induced from the boundary of a framed disc is the connected double
cover: as the boundary tangent turns once, its 2π-rotation lifts from 1 to −1 in Spin(2). We call
the former nonbounding and the latter bounding.
    For a closed oriented spin surface S, the spin quadratic refinement

                                       qS : H1 (S; F2 ) −→ F2

takes a class represented by an embedded circle to zero or one according to whether the induced
spin structure, using its normal line in the surface, is bounding or nonbounding. It satisfies

                                qS (x + y) = qS (x) + qS (y) + (x · y).                         (212)

This is the usual spin quadratic form: resolving transverse intersections adds one tangent turn
per intersection, and the 2π-spin-lift calculation above gives the last term. The well-defined
correspondence between spin structures and such quadratic refinements is given in (Debray and
Gunningham, 2018, Theorem 3.2 and Remark 3.3); its original surface proof is Johnson (1980).

    Here is also the bordism-invariance argument needed for the present obstruction. A spin
bordism has a handle decomposition. An index zero or three handle creates or removes a spin
sphere, whose first homology and Arf invariant are zero. An index one handle either connects two
components, in which case the first-homology quadratic forms add orthogonally, or increases the
genus of one component. In the latter case the new symplectic pair contains the meridian of the
handle. That meridian bounds the cocore disc with its induced spin structure, so its quadratic
value is zero; the pair contributes zero to (213), regardless of the value on its dual. Existing
cycles can be represented outside the attaching discs, so their quadratic values are preserved.
An index two handle is the reverse of an index one handle. Therefore each handle preserves the
total Arf invariant of the boundary, and a spin boundary has Arf invariant zero. This also proves
that a stably framed boundary has Arf invariant zero, because forgetting the framing gives a
spin bordism. The full spin bordism statement is recorded in (Debray and Gunningham, 2018,
Theorem 3.6).
    The intrinsic Lie-torus calculation is the known computation in (Debray and Gunningham,

    e · f = 1,       qM (e) = qM (f ) = 1,             qM (xe + yf ) = x + xy + y,            Arf(M ) = 1.               (214)

Corollary 9.39 (The exact order-two quotient detected by the original cusp map). Let d :

                                                     [β]7→ε(β)
                                 π6 (A, v0 )/ ker ε −−−−−−−→ Z/2.

Every odd multiple of α is nonzero. Its order is either infinite or an even positive integer; this

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; theorem 2.5.

Proof. Postcomposition distributes over the pinch sum on the source sphere, so (p3 )∗ is a group

9.8   An extension homotopy for the angle-forgotten carriers
The literal flat quotient on the punctured cusp need not extend continuously across the central
fibre. Its homotopy class as a map to a torus does extend. This distinction gives a second proof
of the angle-forgotten rank-two nullhomotopy and settles the one-copy circle question left open
in the working-edition homotopy-status remark.

A.1    Classical almost-complex sphere obstructions
Proposition A.1 (Borel–Serre obstruction on S 12 , with three complete proofs). The obstruction
is the classical theorem of Borel and Serre (Borel and Serre, 1953, §15, Proposition 15.1 and the
following remark, p. 434). The complete statement and the three distinct derivations are retained

only the homotopy type of M : the original Borel–Serre reduced-power calculation at the single
prime 5, and Bott integrality. For the standard embedded sphere there is also an independent
stable-tangent Pontryagin-class contradiction.

singular set is not an almost-complex structure on T S 12 and therefore lies outside the hypothesis.

Proposition A.2 (The orientation-compatible almost complex homotopy class). Any two almost
complex structures on the tangent bundle of the smooth six-sphere that induce the same orientation
are homotopic through almost complex structures. Consequently, after an orientation-preserving
diffeomorphism d : S 6 → X, the pulled-back structure d∗ JX is homotopic to the octonionic almost
complex structure with that orientation. The resulting complex rank-three tangent bundles are
isomorphic.

the orientation is preserved. It suffices to compare orthogonal structures.

Theorem A.6 (Credited re-derivation: the smooth side is S 3 × S 3 ). For the sphere twist
data and 0 < |s|  1, the complex-oriented smooth manifold Yu,s is orientation-preservingly
diffeomorphic to S 3 × S 3 . Its integral homology is (Z, 0, 0, Z2 , 0, 0, Z), its middle intersection
form is the rank-two unimodular skew-symmetric form, and w2 = p1 = 0.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; Burklund et al. (2019a); (Kervaire
and Milnor, 1963b, p. 512).

Proof. An ordinary-double-point smoothing replaces a disc neighbourhood of its exceptional
curve by a disc neighbourhood of the vanishing three-sphere. In the displayed coordinates this can
be read without a deformation-theoretic inference: the resolution is the disc bundle of O(−1)⊕2
over S 2 , and the Milnor fibre of the nondegenerate quadratic equation is the disc cotangent
bundle of S 3 . The underlying oriented rank-four bundle over S 2 is trivial, since its w2 is the
reduction of −2 and oriented rank-four bundles over S 2 are classified by π1 SO(4) = Z/2. The
latter disc cotangent bundle is D3 × S 3 because S 3 is parallelizable. Both boundaries are S 2 × S 3 .
    Let A be the complement of the interior of that resolution tube in X log (u) ≃ S 6 . General
position makes A simply connected: a loop and a filling disc in S 6 can be kept disjoint from
the embedded two-sphere since 2 + 2 < 6. Alexander duality gives H       e i (A; Z) = Z for i = 3 and
zero for all other i. The normal three-sphere in the boundary generates that group. In the
Mayer–Vietoris sequence for Y = A ∪ (D3 × S 3 ), the degree-three map from the boundary is
therefore Z → Z2 , with both entries units, and the degree-two boundary group is Z with zero
image. It follows that H2 (Y ) = H4 (Y ) = 0 and that H3 (Y ) is an extension of Z by Z, hence Z2 .
Van Kampen gives π1 (Y ) = 1. The remaining homology follows by duality, and the assertions
about w2 , p1 follow from the vanishing of the corresponding cohomology groups.
    We apply Wall’s classification in the precise form of Burklund–Hahn–Senger, Theorem 2.6,
with their Definition 2.5 and Recollection 2.2 Burklund et al. (2019a). This theorem says that
two (n − 1)-connected closed 2n-manifolds with the same middle intersection form and normal
invariant α : Hn → πn−1 SO(n) differ by a homotopy sphere. Here n = 3, the Hurewicz theorem
gives π2 (Y ) = 0, and π2 SO(3) = 0, so α is zero. Every unimodular skew-symmetric rank-two
form has an oriented symplectic basis; thus these invariants equal those of S 3 × S 3 . Finally
Θ6 /bP7 = 0 by the dimension-six entry of (Kervaire and Milnor, 1963b, p. 512), and bP7 = 0
by its Theorem 5.1 (equivalently the framed-surgery Theorem 6.6). Thus Θ6 = 0 removes the
homotopy-sphere ambiguity. This derives the diffeomorphism assertion from the classification
rather than from Euler characteristic alone.

Theorem A.8 (Credited re-derivation: transverse pullback and the trivial case). Let Y be a
compact complex manifold and h : Y → B a holomorphic map which is a submersion at every
point over p0 , p1 , p2 . Then P = X ×B Y is a compact complex manifold, of dimension dimC Y + 2.
If Y = B × N with its projection, then P ≃ X × N holomorphically, is diffeomorphic to S 6 × N ,
and
         π1 (P ) = π1 (N ), Hk (P ; Z) = Hk (N ; Z) ⊕ Hk−6 (N ; Z), χ(P ) = 2χ(N ).       (E.15)

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; the explicit constructions and
calculations in the proof.

Proof. The pullback is the inverse image of the diagonal under (f, h) : X × Y → B × B. At
any point, either df is onto or its base value is exceptional and dh is onto. Thus the difference
of these two differentials is onto, proving transversality and smoothness. It is a closed subset
of a compact product, hence compact. The maps (x, (t, n)) 7→ (x, n) and (x, n) 7→ (x, (f (x), n))
give the asserted holomorphic identification. The homology statement is the integral Kunneth
theorem with H∗ (S 6 ), which is free; there are no Tor terms. Fundamental groups and Euler
characteristics of products give the remaining formulas.

Proof. The mapping-torus exact sequence, or Proposition A.11, gives H k (M ; Z) = 0 for 2 ≤ k ≤ 5
and H 1 (M ; Z) = Z. The same vanishing in degree two holds with Z/2 coefficients, so M is spin.

the assertions about lifts and determinant trivializations.
      If two lifts of c differ by δα with α ∈ H 1 (M ; Z), the relative cup-product identity gives

assertion here that the relative class c̄ itself is unique.

    A spin coboundary can be supplied using the connected-sum description: bound the product
by S 1 ×D7 and bound the sphere summand by its spin coboundary. Thus no inference from simple
connectivity of M is made; indeed π1 (M ) = Z. The original Eells–Kuiper paper’s unstructured
formulation has an extra condition on H 1 (W ; Z/2) → H 1 (M ; Z/2) to ensure spin structures glue.
Our explicit requirement that the boundary spin structures match supplies precisely that gluing
datum. By Proposition A.11 the two possible spin structures on this particular M have equal
invariant. Finally the splitting principle gives p1 (T W8 ) = c21 − 2c2 for an almost complex tangent

Proposition A.14 (the circle action and local shear). The effective circle subgroup ρ = R/Z ⊂
C/Z of Paper I, Proposition 4.9 and Paper I, Proposition 4.10 and Paper I, Theorem 5.10 acts
freely outside its fixed double curve. That curve is a sphere, and its two complex normal weights
are 1, −1. A monodromy representative may be chosen ρ-equivariant. In marked real coordinates
on a regular torus fibre, its linear part is I − 2δb ⊗ γ; its affine correction is the translation supplied
by Paper I, Proposition 3.3 and Paper I, Proposition 3.4 and Paper I, Theorem 3.8 and depends
on the trivialization.

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; the explicit constructions and
calculations in the proof.
    The fixed sphere, its normal weights, and freeness of the effective circle outside it are
already established in Claude and Alpöge (2026b, Proposition 9.24 and Remark 9.25, pp. 82–83).
The marked period shear and the commuting scalar action are the integer-period-shear and
constructed-action-groupoid formulas of the original version 1 (Du et al., 2026a, Section 7): at
k = −2, Ωa+k = Ωa (I + kE41 ) is the displayed I − 2δb ⊗ γ in the ordered marking. The proof
below retains the explicit equivariant-transport construction. These known formulas do not
evaluate the smooth mapping class of the parameter loop.

Proof. On a regular torus the circle acts by translation in the primitive lattice direction δ,
                                                                                            b and is
therefore free. At a multiple fibre, apply the invariant covector γ to the equation that a circle

Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                      Paper III


translation agrees with the j-th affine deck generator to the power a. Since the deck translation
has γ-component ±1/mj , equality forces a ≡ 0 (mod mj ). Primitivity of δb then forces the circle
element to be the identity. This checks freeness on the quotient using the actual twist vectors,
including the root centre; the argument is not just a statement about the product cover.
    In a cusp toric chart, the relevant primitive edge directions are e1 , e2 , e1 − e2 , with e2 = δ.
                                                                                                    b
Their nonzero determinants with e2 have absolute value one. Thus stabilizers off the edge
in direction e2 are trivial. Along that edge the circle is fixed; the two normal characters in
the adjacent unimodular cones are 1 and −1 because the base monomial is invariant. The
opposite-edge identification gives the double curve with its two distinct triple-point endpoints,
namely a P1 . This verifies the toric step of Paper I, Proposition 4.9 and Paper I, Proposition 4.10
and Paper I, Theorem 5.10 used here.
    The circle acts on the entire family and commutes with the endpoint isomorphism F2 .
Averaging a Riemannian metric over this compact circle makes the orthogonal horizontal
distribution invariant. Its parallel transport and hence the monodromy commute with ρ. On a
local marked torus chart, Πc−2 = Πc (I − 2δb ⊗ γ). Inserting the identity complex-linear part and
translation of Paper I, Proposition 3.3 and Paper I, Proposition 3.4 and Paper I, Theorem 3.8
gives the asserted affine formula. A locally chosen lift of its translation must not be multiplied
by a real interpolation parameter without checking its period cocycle; that operation need not
descend to the torus bundle.
Proposition A.15 (equivariance alone is insufficient). All 28 oriented mapping classes of
S 6 admit representatives equivariant for one fixed semifree circle action with fixed set S 2 .
Consequently the circle action, its fixed set, and its normal weights do not determine [Φ].

Uses: the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; Durán and Rigas (2007, Theorem
2.1).

Proof. Use S 6 ⊂ Im H ⊕ H. The equivariant Blakers–Massey construction gives a generator σ
of π0 Diff+ (S 6 ) equivariant for simultaneous quaternionic conjugation. The smooth reentrance
statement is Durán and Rigas (2007, Theorem 2.1); Section 3.2 identifies this representative
and its powers with all 28 classes. Restrict conjugation to q = eiθ/2 , regarding q and −q as
the same effective circle element. Its fixed vector space consists of p ∈ Ri and w ∈ R + Ri,
a real three-space, so the fixed set on the sphere is S 2 . Outside it, at least one of the two
(j, k)-planes is nonzero, and an effective rotation fixing it is the identity. Thus the action is
semifree. All powers of σ commute with it. Conjugating the complex coordinate on one of the
two real normal planes writes the characters as 1, −1; this representation calculation is checked
exactly in code/c_exact.py. These are statements about smooth circle actions and normal
representations, not a comparison of their complex structures with Xc .

5. The integral cocycle group and actual sections. We spell out the relation between

subgroup (Fukae, 2002, Lemma 4.1, Theorem 4.2 and Corollaries 4.2–4.3, pp. 21–22).

construction and proves that every quotient cocycle is realized by an actual section.
