AI.10.5    Apply the calculation to the tangent bundle

An almost complex structure on S 2n makes its real tangent bundle into a complex rank-n bundle
E. Its top Chern class is the Euler class in the orientation induced by J: both are the signed zero
obstruction of a section of the same oriented real bundle; a complex frame gives the same local
orientation used for the top Chern obstruction. Write σ = 1 or −1 for the sign of this orientation
relative to the outward sphere orientation. Its outward-oriented tangent Euler number is exactly
two, as the following section computes without a general Euler-characteristic theorem. Fix a unit
a ∈ R2n+1 and use the tangent field sa (p) = a − ha, pip. Its only zeros are p = a and p = −a.
Differentiation on the tangent space at either zero is −ha, piI, so the two derivatives are −I and
+I in real dimension 2n, both with determinant sign +1. The zero-count proof in section AI.10.3
gives Euler number two. Reversing the fibre orientation multiplies its class by σ. It follows that

                                            cn (E) = 2σu.                                       (2129)

   Equation (2128) gives (n − 1)! | 2. Thus n ≤ 3.
   We must still exclude n = 2, and the following argument excludes every even n. The full real
stable trivialization is

                    T S 2n ⊕ 1R −→ S 2n × R2n+1 ,        (p; v, a) 7−→ (p; v + ap).             (2130)

     Its inverse sends (p; w) to (p; w −hw, pip, hw, pi). Complexifying it gives (E ⊕ Ē)⊕1C ≃ 12n+1
                                                                                                  C    .
The exact map behind ER ⊗ C ≃ E ⊕ Ē sends v ⊗ z to (zv, zv̄), with scalar multiplication in
the conjugate bundle in the second component. In underlying real notation its inverse on (w, v̄)
is 12 (w + v) ⊗ 1 + 12 J(v − w) ⊗ i. This proves the complexification comparison, including its
conjugate summand; it does not assert that E itself is stably trivial as a complex bundle.
     Conjugation gives cj (Ē) = (−1)j cj (E), since it negates each line Chern root; the equality also
follows from conjugating the unitary curvature in the elementary symmetric Chern polynomial.
Taking total Chern classes of the complexified stable trivialization, and using the dimension of
the sphere, yields

                              1 = c(E)c(Ē) = 1 + (1 + (−1)n )cn (E).                           (2131)

    The term (−1)n cn (E)2 is in degree 4n, which is zero on the 2n-sphere; this is its exact
reason for vanishing. If n is even, (2131) says 2cn (E) = 0, contradicting (2129) in the free group
H 2n (S 2n ; Z). Hence only n = 1, 3 remain.


                                                 889
Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                           Paper III


    Both are realized. The complex atlas of CP1 , identified with S 2 by (2125) in dimension
two, provides n = 1. Formula (2054) provides n = 3; its failure of integrability does not affect
the almost-complex assertion. With our original octonion labels, the orientation calculation
after (2062) gives σ = −1, so its top Chern class is −2u in the outward orientation, and its top
Chern character is −u by (2127). An odd-dimensional real tangent space cannot carry J 2 = −1,
because it would be a complex vector space and thus have even real dimension. This proves the
claimed classification of positive-dimensional spheres. The zero-sphere consists of two complex
zero-dimensional points and is outside that stated range.

AI.11     Six complete exercises
AI.11.1     Exercise 1. Keep the algebra and orientation comparisons together

Prove that the map Φ in (2042) preserves cross products and associators, and compute its
determinant on the imaginary seven-space.
    Solution. It preserves the real unit, the inner product, and multiplication by (2042)–(2043).
Applying it to xy = −hx, yi + x × y therefore gives Φ(x × y) = Φ(x) ×? Φ(y). Applying it
separately to the two bracketed products in (2063) gives Φ([x, y, z]O ) = [Φx, Φy, Φz]? . In the
basis (1, e1 , . . . , e7 ), it fixes the first quaternion and the real coordinate of the second quaternion,
and negates its three imaginary coordinates. Its full determinant is (−1)3 = −1. Since the
real unit is fixed, the determinant on its perpendicular imaginary space is also −1. Thus the
induced sphere map reverses the specified ambient outward orientations while intertwining the
two corresponding almost complex fields. Their complex orientations are transported by the
intertwining differential, as follows directly from the ordered bases (v1 , Jv1 , . . . , v3 , Jv3 ). There
is no conflict between these two orientation statements: the ambient and complex orientations
have each been specified separately and compared by explicit determinants.

AI.11.2     Exercise 2. Describe every fixed-vector obstruction map, including its zero
            case

For NU in (2066), determine its kernel and image, solve NU V = W when it is solvable, and
include U = 0.
    Solution. If U 6= 0, equations (2068)–(2070) give kernel spanR (U, JU ), image WU , and the
particular solution

                                               NU W
                                      V0 = −              (W ∈ WU ).                                (2132)
                                               16|U |2
    Indeed applying NU gives W by (2069). All solutions are V0 + aU + bJU , a, b ∈ R, because
their differences are exactly the kernel. A vector with nonzero component in span(U, JU ) is not
in the image. If U = 0, bilinearity gives N0 = 0, its kernel is the entire tangent space, its image
is zero, and the equation has every V as a solution for W = 0 and no solution otherwise. No
division in (2132) is applied to this zero case.

AI.11.3     Exercise 3. Determine all scalar holomorphic functions for the octonion
            field

Let U ⊂ S 6 be a connected open subset, and let f : U → C be a C 2 function satisfying df ◦J = i df
for the field (2054). Prove that f is constant.
    Solution. The equation says ∂¯J f = 0. Hence ∂¯J2 f = 0. By (2036), df annihilates the image
of N . Equation (2074) says that image is the entire TJ1,0 , while the original equation says that
df annihilates TJ0,1 . Their direct sum is the complexified tangent bundle, so df = 0. The function


                                                    890
Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                                          Paper III


is locally constant, and connectedness makes it constant on U . In the adapted frame the precise
equations are

            (∂¯J2 f )(Z̄2 , Z̄3 ) = iZ1 f,    (∂¯J2 f )(Z̄3 , Z̄1 ) = iZ2 f,   (∂¯J2 f )(Z̄1 , Z̄2 ) = iZ3 f.     (2133)
    This is stronger than the assertion that this field supplies no holomorphic coordinate system.
More generally the same proof applies to any almost complex structure for which the image of
the complex tensor map in (2071) spans T 1,0 at every point of the open set. It proves that exact
consequence; it does not assert the same condition for a different field on the sphere.

AI.11.4    Exercise 4. Test the coordinate-change sign without discarding nonlinear
           terms

In complex dimension one, take A = 0, real , and H(z) = z + z z̄. Compute E = B ◦ H, the
real Jacobian, and Ψ = (∂ζ B) ◦ H wherever the displayed inverses exist.
    Solution. Here H̄ = z̄ + z z̄, so (2084) gives
                             z
                 E=−              ,          jH = (1 + z̄)(1 + z) − 2 z z̄ = 1 + (z + z̄).                    (2134)
                           1 + z
    The cancelled quadratic terms are displayed in the determinant. The inverse real Jacobian
gives (∂ζ H −1 ) ◦ H = (1 + z)/jH . The expression E is holomorphic in z, so its z̄-derivative is
zero. Therefore
                                                             
                                        Ψ=−                               .                                       (2135)

    For example, on |z| < 1/4 both denominators are nonzero and the real Jacobian is positive.
The first variation is −1, in agreement with − 14 ∆(z z̄) = −1. This local test is not the periodic
coordinate choice in section AI.7; it verifies the sign using the original nonlinear formula on its

AI.11.5    Exercise 5. See the intermediate cohomology which the collapse does not
           remove

On S 2 × S 2 , expand the full K-class and Chern character of Q1 ⊗ Q2 , and compare with a
pullback from S 4 under (2125).
    Solution. Since [Qi ] = 1 + bi ,

            [Q1 ⊗ Q2 ] = 1 + b1 + b2 + b1 b2 ,               ch(Q1 ⊗ Q2 ) = 1 − u1 − u2 + u1 u2 .                 (2136)
    The two degree-two terms are nonzero: they pair as −1 with the respective factor spheres.
A bundle of rank r on S 4 has Chern character r − c2 by (2127), so its pullback has the form
r − mu1 u2 for an integer m; it has no degree-two component. Thus the line in (2136) is not such
a pullback. The map f ∗ identifies the top generators exactly but does not make the product’s
intermediate classes disappear. This is the concrete distinction needed in the sphere proof.

AI.11.6    Exercise 6. Conjugate the actual almost complex field

Compute N−J , the complex orientation, and the top Chern class for the negative of the field
(2054), preserving the outward orientation of the labelled sphere.
    Solution. Substitute −J in all four terms of (2031). The first term has two minus signs in
its bracket, and each of the last two terms has one minus sign from the outer endomorphism and
one from the inner vector. Consequently

                                                          891
Sphere maps and manifold constructions                                                           Paper III




                                                 N−J = NJ .                                        (2137)

   The ordered real complex basis changes as

                   (v1 , Jv1 , v2 , Jv2 , v3 , Jv3 ) 7−→ (v1 , −Jv1 , v2 , −Jv2 , v3 , −Jv3 ).

Its orientation therefore changes by (−1)3 = −1. Since the original field has sign −1 relative to
the outward orientation, the conjugate has sign +1. Its complex tangent bundle is the conjugate
bundle of the original one, so c3 changes from −2u to +2u, and ch3 = c3 /2 changes from −u
to +u. The nonzero tensor in (2137) remains, so this conjugate field is also not integrable. The
calculation changes an orientation and a Chern sign without changing the zero condition of the
actual tensor.

AK      Programs, finite certificates and portable commands
All paths below are relative to the companion archive root. Change to the displayed working
directory and run the displayed command. The output column identifies the retained output of
the recorded execution; a replay may print to the terminal or update its own explicitly named
JSON/TOML certificate. The complete execution catalogue is records/III_program_inde
x.json. It preserves each original command when recorded, all source and output hashes,
supplementary runs, unsuccessful attempts and their resolutions. The indexer does not execute
mathematical programs.
    The recorded Python environment is Python 3.12.14, SymPy 1.14.0 and NumPy 2.3.5 where
those packages are imported. Standard-library-only checkers do not need either package. For
the Python dependencies, run python3 -m pip install sympy==1.14.0 numpy==2.3.5
in a suitable environment. Keep the archived directory structure: the reconstructed MAPS
projects include their original imported engines and exact JSON fixtures. The Julia tests use
Julia 1.10.10, Hecke 0.41.1, Nemo 0.57.2 and AbstractAlgebra 0.51.4. Their pinned project and
manifest are in code/root_maps_F/runtime/hecke_env. Install Julia and instantiate that
environment by running julia --startup-file=no --project=hecke_env -e 'using Pkg;
Pkg.instantiate()' from code/root_maps_F/runtime. Runtime binaries and package caches
are not included. The direct Julia commands below replace the historical run_hecke.py launcher,
which contains a machine-specific cache path; the actual historical launcher invocation remains
in the execution record.
    These are finite, symbolic or per-input checks. A successful output does not prove a geometric
identification, a topological realization, an all-stage comparison theorem or an exhaustive
enumeration of an infinite class set. The complete proofs and the exact finite ranges are given
at the receiving statements. Imported implementations are identified with the test driver that
actually called them. Repeated checks of the same unchanged program with identical arguments
are consolidated in the table; every recorded run remains separately available in the JSON
catalogue.

Open problem AL.1 (Open: the full filling and smooth classification). The natural section-line
sphere question is complete on all 21 profiles, with 59 marked sphere patterns on 50 initial
rows (4.33–28). 4.38–33 compute every allowed finite affine logarithm and every original/log
additive and original/Mumford multiplicative choice on the natural initial catalogue: 495 integral
presentations on 172 initial rows. 4.46, 4.49 and 4.50 include every positive translation iterate,
retaining shared even factors, arbitrary free finite and regular logarithms and the ordinary
clutch. 4.52 supplies the full nonsaturated general-cusp boundary kernel. 4.55 now removes the
scalar-iterate restriction: all positive section pairs satisfying the fibrewise narrowness condition
and every effective whole-fibre weight distribution on multiplicative or regular fibres have a
complete integral algorithm, with the original star caps. The exceptional OS49/II Klein-four
vertical subgroup is retained in the actual fundamental group.
    The entire specified minimal simply connected smooth sector is now classified: all 162
patterns, all their allowed finite logarithmic orders and affine twists, and every simply connected
ordinary clutch, within the stated primitive-Mumford scope and without additional regular
logarithms. 4.53–45 resolve the last 18 patterns. Residual orders 4, 8, 20 give respectively Z4,1 ,
Z8,0 and Z4,1 #Z5,1 . Their full refined classes are 2, 0, 14 in the fixed cyclic coordinates, and
their fundamental-class invariants are zero. The actual relative spin calculation uses the rational
linking of the literal critical cycle. The preferred finite-II core three-manifold is a full torsion
generator even when the ordinary regular three-torus is not. No division of an even cyclic residue
or unproved general change-of-three-frame formula is used.
    4.57 gives the complete oriented smooth classification of the simply connected weighted
Engel family for every positive weight, including its full finite-coefficient fundamental-class
invariant. 4.58 computes all canonical primitive-long-circle odd-star logarithmic caps and their
actual integral boundary kernels. 4.59 proves that component corrections to the initial line exist
exactly when the height product is integral, and constructs sixteen new simply connected fillings.
4.60 computes every invariant-Chern original additive cap, retaining its integral orbit-torsion
extension; its full marked columns are proved when that torsion vanishes. 4.61 consequently
extends the global integral algorithm to every positive initial pair with integral height and the
stated corrected filling choices. It does not replace unresolved torsion-valued boundary columns
by rational or saturated maps.
    The full D.2 request remains open for nonprimitive-long-circle and other logarithmic star data,
corrected original multiplicative caps, and the mixed elliptic–γ and second fixed-normal torsion
columns of the original additive caps when h > 1 in 4.60. The complete smooth invariants of the
remaining weighted and additional-regular-log outputs are also undetermined. For example, 4.55
constructs the simply connected OS45/default member with P = 2G, Q = 8G, weight 2 at I8 ,
all other weights zero, all Mumford caps and ordinary clutch e = 1. It has

                          H2 = Z15 ⊕ Z/8,        H3 = Z/8,       χ = 32.

For this exact example 4.62 computes the complete primitive integral cubic and every coordinate
of the fundamental-class invariant. The component lattice has index two; the primitive extension
and the full boundary coefficient-extension data are retained. Its absolute c1 , c2 , λ vanish. The
sole remaining smooth invariant for this example is the refined class 0 versus 4 in Z/8. An actual
order-two angular boundary cycle bounds on both sides of the cusp and gives an odd class in
H3 (X); its embedded representative, reference framing and critical-specialization linking are not
computed here. Even coefficients in an absolute critical nullchain do not by themselves settle that
